name: ADA4625-1 / ADA4625-2 (ADI 36 V low-noise JFET-input, rail-to-rail output)
tagline: ADI's 36 V JFET-input op-amp: 3.3 nV/rtHz, 18 MHz GBW and rail-to-rail output. diyAudio and Head-Fi users like it for I/V, headphone and phono stages.
technology: Precision JFET-input op-amp. Runs from a single +5 V to +36 V supply (±2.5 V to ±18 V). Input common-mode range includes the negative supply, and the output swings rail to rail. 3.3 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, 18 MHz GBW, 48 V/us, 4 mA per amplifier. 8-lead SOIC with exposed pad (EPAD).

part_numbers.notes: Single. 8-lead SOIC_N_EP. First released with the Rev 0 datasheet (10/2017). Orderable code ADA4625-1ARDZ (the eval board is EVAL-ADA4625-1ARDZ). The reel suffixes and any B grade were not checked.

part_numbers.status: Active (ADI product page live, stocked at Mouser; lifecycle label not re-checked)
part_numbers.notes: Dual. 8-lead SOIC_N_EP. Added in the combined ADA4625-1/ADA4625-2 datasheet (Rev A). Orderable code ADA4625-2ARDZ (Mouser listing). Eval board EVAL-ADA4625-2ARDZ.

lineage.notes: ADA4625-1 datasheet Rev 0 (initial version) is dated 10/2017. The dual ADA4625-2 came with the combined Rev A datasheet (by mid-2019). Rev B is dated 03/2025 and was accompanied by PCN 25_0070 (package outline drawing). There are no second sources.

key_specs.value: Input CM range includes V-; rail-to-rail output

reputation.summary: A niche modern pick with a small base of forum reports. On diyAudio, one member used it as a DAC I/V converter and was 'amazed by the sound quality, almost like a CFA op amp' (OPA828 vs OPA627 thread). On Head-Fi, a poster in The Opamp Thread 'really liked it' in a headphone amp, citing a 'great clean sound' that 'seems to help low end a lot'. diyAudio also has dedicated threads on its 3.3 nV/rtHz spec and on phono-preamp use. One rolling comment calls it a good JFET option but 'somewhat cold'. All of these are individual listener impressions, not measurements.
sonic_descriptors: 'almost like a CFA op amp' (diyAudio I/V user)
caveats: Only sold in an exposed-pad SOIC-8. Rolling it into DIP-8 sockets needs an adapter, and the adapter should handle the EPAD thermally and electrically as the datasheet directs.
The 18 MHz GBW, fast part can oscillate on long adapter leads or with poor decoupling.
It draws about 4 mA per amplifier, so it runs warmer than low-power JFET parts.
The praise comes from a few individual forum posts, and the tonal descriptors contradict each other.

silicon_changes.when: 2025 (datasheet Rev B 03/2025; Mouser lists a PCN dated 2025-06-26)
silicon_changes.identification: ADI PCN 25_0070 compares the old and new package outline drawings. Check the date code against the PCN effective date, and check the package drawing in datasheet Rev B against Rev A.
silicon_changes.summary: PCN 25_0070 covers a package outline drawing change and a datasheet revision for the 8-lead SOIC with exposed pad. Nothing found suggests a die or electrical change, but the PCN body (assembly site, leadframe, EPAD size) was not read.

spec_deltas.after: Revised outline in datasheet Rev B / PCN 25_0070 (exact dimensional changes unconfirmed)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected, because this is a package or documentation change with no die change indicated.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - package outline change only. If the design depends on the exposed-pad land pattern or the fit of a DIP adapter, check the footprint.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports were found. It is a single-source, niche ADI part in an exposed-pad SOIC, so buy from authorized distributors (ADI, DigiKey, Mouser, Arrow/Verical). Treat cheap DIP-adapter 'upgrade' modules from marketplaces with caution.

claims_confirmed: The current ADA4625-1/ADA4625-2 datasheet is Rev B, dated 03/03/2025 on the ADI product page: https://www.analog.com/en/products/ada4625-2.html

The Rev A combined datasheet survives on Verical (https://www.verical.com/datasheet/analog-devices-amplifier-ic-development-tools-EVAL-ADA4625-1ARDZ-5229613.pdf) and on RadioLocman (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=166129, uploaded 2019-07-02).
The ADA4625-1 datasheet revision history shows '10/2017 - Revision 0: Initial Version': https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=166129
Typical specs are 18 MHz GBW, 48 V/us, 3.3 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, ±80 uV max Vos and ±15 pA Ib at 25°C, 5 V to 36 V supply, and -40°C to +125°C: https://www.analog.com/en/products/ada4625-1.html
ADA4625-1 is listed as Recommended for New Designs: https://www.analog.com/en/products/ada4625-1.html

The part draws 4 mA per amplifier, its input CM range includes the negative supply, it has a rail-to-rail output, and it comes in an 8-lead SOIC with EPAD: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ada4625-1-4625-2.pdf

ADI PCN 25_0070 is a package outline drawing comparison for ADA4625-1/ADA4625-2: https://www.analog.com/media/en/PCN/ADI_PCN_25_0070_Rev_-_ADA4625-1%20_%20ADA4625-2%20Package%20Outline%20Drawing%20Comparision.pdf
Mouser lists a PCN dated 2025-06-26 for ADA4625-2ARDZ: https://www.mouser.com/ProductDetail/Analog-Devices/ADA4625-2ARDZ?qs=P1JMDcb91o7LZpOHm1xoQA%3D%3D
